interface.name: nullspace_controller_v1

description.summary: control interface for the Nullspace compositor

interface.description:
This interface lets a client inspect and control the Nullspace compositor: read and write runtime configuration, switch spaces and layouts, manage windows, and query displays, input devices and layer surfaces. Every request is a privileged compositor operation. The interface is intended for trusted, user-run tools only.
Every non-destructor request takes a 32-bit serial argument. The serial must be nonzero; serial zero is reserved for unsolicited broadcast batches. The compositor terminates every batch with exactly one done event, carrying the serial of the request that produced it (or zero for a broadcast). An error, when present, precedes the done of the same batch and carries the same serial.
A client that sends one request and waits for done(its_serial) always observes exactly its own reply, even when broadcasts from other clients or the user are interleaved in the event stream. A client may also use wl_display.roundtrip to ensure that all pending events have been processed before continuing.
Window IDs are assigned by the compositor, are only meaningful within one compositor session, and may be reused after window_removed has been sent.
Every bound controller receives state-change notifications whether it asked for them. Broadcast batches end with done(0), there is no subscribe request.
All strings are UTF-8 (never NULL, but length zero is allowed), and some are controlled by other clients (window titles, app ids, layer namespaces, device names). Treat them as untrusted data (they may contain control characters or terminal escape sequences, and must be sanitized before being written to a terminal.
Requests that do not name an output operate on the output the compositor considers focused (typically the one containing the focused window, or the last one the user interacted with). In a single-output session, this is the only output. Requests that operate on spaces, layouts, or the focused window inherit this target.

entry.name: invalid_serial
entry.summary: serial was zero or reused while still in flight

enum.name: key_type

description.summary: value type of a configuration key

enum.description: All configuration values travel as strings. The type tells the client how to parse and format them.

enum.name: status

description.summary: non-fatal status codes for the error event

enum.description:
Reported via the error event for application-level failures. The connection remains usable. Fatal protocol violations are reported with wl_resource_post_error (see the error enum) and do close the connection.
Every error event is immediately followed by a done event carrying the same serial.

entry.name: invalid_value
entry.description: A value failed to parse or was out of range, or an index/layout name was not valid. The error message describes the problem.

entry.name: not_supported

description.summary: request cannot be served in this state

entry.description: The request is valid but cannot be satisfied right now or for this key. Examples: reading a per-space key through get_config (use get_space_info instead), or show_binding_help while the overview is active.

entry.name: locked
entry.description: The session is locked. Requests that modify state are rejected (read-only queries are not currently rejected).

description.summary: window id is not valid in this session

entry.name: mapped
entry.description: The window has a buffer attached. A window on a hidden space or a minimized window can still be reported as mapped.

entry.name: floating
entry.description: The window is transient, or its space uses a non-tiling layout.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroys the object. The client stops receiving events. No done is sent for this request.

request.name: get_config
request.description: Replies with config_value and done, or with error (unknown_key or not_supported) and done. Per-space keys (space_window_count or space_urgent) are not readable this way and yield not_supported (use get_space_info instead).

request.name: set_config
request.description:
On success, the compositor broadcasts config_value. The broadcast uses serial zero.
On failure, replies with error and done carrying this request's serial: unknown_key, read_only, invalid_value (parse failure or out of range), or locked. The error message names the key and the reason. A failed write changes nothing.
Boolean values are exactly "true" or "false", numbers are range-checked against the range reported by config_key, color keys take "#rrggbb" or "#rrggbbaa".

request.name: restore_last

description.summary: restore the most recently minimized window

request.description: Broadcasts the same batch as window_minimize. It is not an error if there is nothing to restore.

request.name: show_binding_help

description.summary: show the on-screen key binding help

request.description: Asks the compositor to show the on-screen key binding panel.

event.name: window_removed
event.description: Broadcast when a window is closed, followed by done(0). After this event, the ID must be considered as invalid.

event.name: error

description.summary: non-fatal error reported for a request

event.description: Sent when a request could not be satisfied for an application-level reason. The client may continue using the interface. Fatal protocol violations use wl_resource_post_error instead. The message is for humans and its wording is not stable. Always followed by done with the same serial.

event.name: done

description.summary: end of a batch of events

event.description:
Terminates a batch. The compositor sends exactly one done after every non-destructor request, whether it succeeded or failed, and after every unsolicited notification batch.
A done carrying a nonzero serial terminates the reply to the request that uses that serial (all events since the previous done in the same direction belong to that reply). A done carrying serial zero terminates an unsolicited broadcast batch.
Every broadcast batch is a complete unit. Clients that issue a single request and exit may wait for any done reply whose serial matches theirs (or "use wl_display.roundtrip").

arg.name: space
arg.summary: -1 = window is not assigned to a space
